lane: v0.7.0 news lane: OD-3 / O-05 news rendering budget (ADR-041)

code.after: c64d8d5: fd3b69d (render allowance, blocking, static-first, news_rendering switch), d26a882 (encyclopedia and out-of-window pages after dated news), c64d8d5 (SearXNG news interleaved by engine; hits dated before the window fetched last)

environment.host: DGX Spark class host (GB10, 121 GiB MemTotal unified memory, 20 cores); memory pressure 'ok' during the runs (about 36 GiB available)
environment.searxng: shared SearXNG on 127.0.0.1:8888 (loopback JSON API, honest User-Agent)
environment.model: shared vLLM on 127.0.0.1:8811 (nsf llm config --url http://127.0.0.1:8811/v1 --reasoning)
environment.browser: Playwright with system Chromium /usr/bin/chromium; Chromium sandbox on; every sub-request through SafeFetcher (robots.txt, address policy, Retry-After, honest User-Agent)
environment.individual: fresh scratch database <scratch>/lane_news_live/ind.sqlite (not the owner's instance): `nsf init`, `nsf web config --enable --set searxng_url=...`, model configured; every other setting default, so browser_rendering false and news_rendering true (the new default)

summary: A render is one page read of the task plus its own allowance of budget.max_render_requests sub-requests (default 100, ceiling 150), tallied in usage.render_requests, never charged to max_requests (20 in a quick lookup).

Renders per task: max_browser_sessions (1; ceiling 2). Renders per UTC day: daily_renders 40, a meta counter forgetting does not refund. Refused at critical memory pressure and with under 10 s of the time budget left.
Never fetched: images, media, fonts, stylesheets, beacons, 'other' (favicons, prefetches), iframes, and known ad/analytics hosts (browser.BLOCKED_DOMAINS).

Static-first for news questions: dated, in-window static pages first; pages without text (rendered when allowed), undated pages, encyclopedia articles and out-of-window pages or hits after them. SearXNG news results interleaved by engine. Search-engine dates order candidates only and never date a source.
news_rendering on by default (owner switch `nsf web config --no-news-render`), only for questions a person asked; general browser_rendering stays off by default.

method: request counts: one BrowserRenderer.render per URL through a SafeFetcher with the honest User-Agent, before (94ccb09 renderer: one budget, stylesheets/iframes/trackers fetched) and after (blocking + allowance; allowance raised to 400 for measurement so nothing was cut). sub_requests excludes the page's own robots.txt and page fetch. Sites: msn.com (Bing News's main source) and three other news sites whose robots.txt admits the honest User-Agent for the article path: finance.yahoo.com, foxbusiness.com, wccftech.com. Their static HTML already has text and a JSON-LD date, so the product does not render them; they are measured for the request count only

memory: summed RSS and summed PSS of the Playwright driver and every Chromium process, sampled every 0.2 s; RSS double-counts shared pages, PSS does not; child_cpu_s from os.times() of the reaped driver

live: `nsf web ask "What happened in AI this week?"` three times and `nsf web ask "What is the latest news about NVIDIA?"` once, default (auto) mode -> quick_lookup budget (3 pages, 3 queries, 20 requests, 1 browser session, 100 render sub-requests, 45 s); wall_ms from the shell around the CLI process

date_obtained_from: the extractor's date_source of the stored source (json-ld = JSON-LD datePublished in the static or rendered HTML; meta:article:published_time = OpenGraph article meta in the rendered DOM); search-engine dates are not source dates
text_chars: the stored body (public cache) re-extracted
an exploratory run on d26a882's parent (fd3b69d) is summarised under exploratory_run; the four reported runs are on the final code

summary.msn.com: 76 and 80 sub-requests before; after: 78, 76, 81, 76 (probes), 75, 25, 75, 69 (final live runs) and 72, 72, 79 (live runs on d26a882); the 25 was a render whose page stopped loading early (text, no date). MSN assembles the article from about 60 first-party script chunks on assets.msn.com, which no blocking can remove; blocking removes the ad/analytics hosts, the login iframe and their robots.txt fetches (about 5-8) but the page then loads a few more first-party chunks. Fits the 100 allowance in every run.
summary.foxbusiness.com: 76 -> 34-36 (ads, ad-tech scripts and stylesheets no longer fetched)
summary.finance.yahoo.com: 246 -> 236 (about 230 first-party script chunks); exceeds the allowance, but its static HTML carries text and a JSON-LD date, so it is never rendered

request_counts.chromium_resources: peak per render: summed PSS 427-534 MiB, summed RSS 1.2-1.4 GiB, 3-5 s of CPU over 10-20 s wall

exploratory_run.question: What happened in AI this week?
exploratory_run.what_happened: two Wikipedia articles (read first as encyclopedia hits) and artificialintelligence-news.com's home page dated 2020-03-19 (JSON-LD) filled the 3 page slots; the MSN article waiting for a render was never reached (0 renders, 15 requests). Fixed by d26a882 (encyclopedia and out-of-window pages after the dated news pages).
exploratory_run.second_exploratory_runs: on d26a882 the three AI runs met freshness (msn.com rendered, 72/72/79 sub-requests); the NVIDIA run did not: SearXNG kept 8 of 40 news results, all Hacker News threads, and a 2022 thread was read and rendered (reason undated_news, 1 sub-request). Fixed by c64d8d5.

bench.result: every metric identical (retrieval 12/12, coverage 21/24, top answer 9/12, citation precision 193/194, freshness 8/8, verdicts 29/29, contradiction P/R 1.0/0.8571, recall@3 1.0, identical across 3 runs); only resource noise changed (peak RSS +3 to +4 %, per-task DB growth within +-4 KiB, task wall p50 +7 % on a shared host). The offline bench renders nothing: its fixture questions never reach the render gate

findings: All 4 live runs met the freshness requirement with dated, cited sources (AI x3: 7-day window; NVIDIA: 2-day volatile window). Before (news_render_live.json, default config) the same AI question ended 'freshness requirement not met' with 0 sources with text.

Each run rendered exactly one msn.com article (reason js_shell) within its own allowance (75, 25, 75 and 69 sub-requests of 100, never exhausted) and spent 9-16 of the task's 20 requests on discovery and static pages; no render was cut short.

Dates came from the publishers' own markup: JSON-LD datePublished in static HTML (yahoo.com, newsweek.com) and article:published_time in MSN's rendered DOM. In run 2 the rendered MSN page (25 sub-requests) carried text but no date; freshness was met by the static yahoo.com page.

Robots and site rules held: www.reuters.com blocked_robots, news.ycombinator.com rate_limited by its 30 s Crawl-delay (not waited out), usatoday.com HTTP 402 and nytimes.com HTTP 403 not retried or bypassed; 1-2 MSN sub-requests per render refused by robots.txt (api.msn.com LiveRamp) and left refused.

Wall time 36-42 s against the quick lookup's 45 s; the render step (deferred static reads plus the render) took 9-16 s of it, the model answer most of the rest. The model answer was written in all 4 runs (1-3 sentences accepted by the guard).
limitations: Four runs on one evening; live rankings change from minute to minute (three of the AI runs read the same MSN article).
Every answer cluster is single-source; current events rarely get a second independent source within 3 pages.

A page whose article needs more than 100 sub-requests (Yahoo Finance, about 236) would render incomplete and the report says so; such pages are rendered only when their static HTML has no text or date.
news_rendering runs Chromium on untrusted news-site JavaScript by default once web access is enabled (sandboxed, at most 1 per task and 40 per day).
